task.title: Reset a user’s OTP credential in Keycloak
task.shortdesc: When a user loses or replaces the phone that holds their authenticator app, sign the user out, delete the phone’s one-time password (OTP) credential, and make the user set up a new one at their next sign-in. This resets the OTP credential only: it doesn’t remove passkeys, security keys or other second factors that the user may also have.

ul.li: Confirm that the request comes from the user. Use a phone number or an address the user gave before they lost the phone, not one in the request.
Sign in to the admin console with an account that can manage the realm’s users. The screenshots were taken as an administrator of the master realm.
Make sure that the user has the new phone, with an authenticator app such as FreeOTP, Google Authenticator, or Microsoft Authenticator.
Check that the realm uses Keycloak’s default browser flow, in which the OTP step is conditional. With a custom flow, Keycloak may ask for a code at a different point, or not at all.

prereq.note: Do the steps in this order. Sign the user out first: an open session reaches Mobile Authenticator Setup without asking for the password. Then add the required action before you delete the credential: in the other order, the user can sign in with the password alone in between. I tested both on Keycloak 26.8.2.

context.p: For Keycloak administrators. Written for Keycloak 26.8.2 and checked against it. Every screen here comes from a Keycloak 26.8.2 server running on my own computer, with a test realm and test users. This is an independent guide, not official Keycloak documentation.

step.cmd: In the admin console, check that the user’s realm is the current realm: its name is at the top of the menu. Select Users, search for the user, and then select their username.

image.alt: The Users page of the admin console. The search box is outlined in green, and the username alex.morgan is outlined and marked 1.

step.cmd: On the Sessions tab, select Logout all sessions, and then select Confirm. The dialog says that it signs out “active subjects in this realm.” On a user’s Sessions tab, it signs out that user only. In a test with a second user, the second user’s session stayed open.

image.alt: The Sessions tab of alex.morgan, marked 1, with one open session in the list. The Logout all sessions button is outlined and marked 2.

step.cmd: On the Details tab, in Required user actions, select Configure OTP, and then select Save.

image.alt: The Details tab of alex.morgan. Configure OTP is selected in Required user actions, marked 1, and the Save button is marked 2.

step.cmd: Select the Credentials tab, and find the Otp row of the lost phone: its User label names the device, such as Alex’s phone. If the user has more than one Otp row, delete only the row of the lost phone.

image.alt: The Credentials tab, marked 1, with two rows, Password and Otp. The Otp row, labelled Alex’s phone, is outlined and marked 2.

step.cmd: In that Otp row, open the menu at the end of the row, and then select Delete.

image.alt: The menu of the Otp row is open, and its Delete item is outlined and marked 1.

step.cmd: In the Delete credentials? dialog, select Delete. Check that the Otp row of the lost phone no longer appears on the Credentials tab.

image.alt: The Delete credentials? dialog over the Credentials tab. Its red Delete button is outlined and marked 1.

step.cmd: Ask the user to sign in. After the password, Keycloak shows Mobile Authenticator Setup. The user scans the QR code with the authenticator app on the new phone, enters the code that the app shows, names the device, and then selects Submit.

image.alt: The Mobile Authenticator Setup page that the user sees. The one-time code field, the device name field and the Submit button are marked 1 to 3. The QR code is covered because it contains the secret.

result.p: On the Sessions tab, no session is listed. On the Credentials tab, a new Otp row shows the name that the user gave the new device, with today’s date.

image.alt: The Credentials tab with a new Otp row, labelled Alex’s new phone, outlined and marked 1.

result.p: Keycloak also keeps a record. When the realm saves admin events, Events > Admin events lists the deletion as an ACTION on the user’s credential, and the new required action as an UPDATE of the user.

image.alt: Admin events, with the ACTION on the user’s credential outlined.

postreq.note: If the phone was stolen, or the password may be known to someone else, also select Update Password in step 3. The user then sets a new password before setting up the authenticator.

ul.li: If Invalid authenticator code. appears during the setup, see When a Keycloak user can’t sign in with a one-time password.
To see what the realm asks of an authenticator, such as the number of digits and how long a code lasts, see Keycloak OTP policy.
